# Study overview

[Cahyadi et al. (2020)](https://doi.org/10.1257/pol.20190245) studied Indonesia's
conditional cash transfer program after six years of randomized rollout. Their
IV estimates indicated increases of 23.3 percentage points in skilled birth
attendance and 17.1 points in facility delivery. Here original subdistrict
assignment instruments household PKH receipt by 2013. We compare the published
estimates with reconstructed 2SLS and princeBART complier effects, then summarize
heterogeneity across baseline household characteristics. The analysis concerns
recorded deliveries among surveyed women, not every woman in the original cohort.
The [paper](Cahyadi_2020.pdf) is retained locally.

# Dataset

```{r load-data}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(ivreg)
  library(sandwich)
  library(princeBART)
  library(future)
  library(posterior)
})

load("processed_data.rda")
head(dat, 5)
```

- **Outcomes:** `good_assisted_delivery` and `delivery_facility`, both binary.
- **Treatment:** `pkh_by_this_wave`, household PKH receipt by the 2013 wave.
- **Instrument:** `L07`, original randomized rollout assignment.
- **Covariates:** baseline household-head occupation/education, housing,
  water/sanitation, electricity, household size, expenditure, and missingness
  indicators. `kabupaten` supplies district adjustment; `kecamatan` identifies
  the subdistrict clusters. Linkage and pregnancy-source fields are not predictors.

## Common sample and model specification

Retain the authors' baseline coding and district adjustment. Constant predictors
are omitted. Both outcomes use the same complete-case sample; multiple records
from one mother remain, as in the pregnancy-record construction.

```{r prepare-analysis}
baseline_controls <- grep("_baseline_(nm|miss)$", names(dat), value = TRUE)
required <- c("good_assisted_delivery", "delivery_facility", "L07",
              "pkh_by_this_wave", "kabupaten", "kecamatan", baseline_controls)
dat <- dat[complete.cases(dat[required]), ] |> droplevels()
baseline_controls <- baseline_controls[vapply(dat[baseline_controls],
  function(x) n_distinct(x) > 1L, logical(1))]
covariate_rhs <- paste(c("kabupaten", baseline_controls), collapse = " + ")
# Remove redundant linear controls from the IV formula, preserving their span.
control_matrix <- model.matrix(as.formula(paste("~", covariate_rhs)), data = dat)
control_qr <- qr(control_matrix)
independent <- colnames(control_matrix)[control_qr$pivot[seq_len(control_qr$rank)]]
iv_covariate_rhs <- paste(c("kabupaten", intersect(baseline_controls, independent)), collapse = " + ")
settings <- list(n_chains = 4L, workers = 4L, n_warmup = 500L,
                 n_samples = 750L, n_trees = 50L)
```

The common sample contains **`r nrow(dat)` delivery records** in
**`r n_distinct(dat$kecamatan)` subdistricts**. Instrument propensity is estimated
internally. IV standard errors are clustered by subdistrict. princeBART uses the
same predictors flexibly, but its likelihood does not adjust for clustering.
The credible intervals therefore do not represent cluster-adjusted uncertainty.
Redundant dummy and missingness-indicator columns are omitted from the IV formula;
the linear adjustment space is unchanged.

## Estimation and comparison

The shared function fits both methods, computes 95% intervals and MCMC diagnostics,
and produces a shallow-tree heterogeneity summary. Effects are reported in
percentage points. Published intervals are reconstructed from rounded clustered
SEs in Table 2; these are marginal intervals, not Romano--Wolf-adjusted intervals.
The original randomization, exclusion, and monotonicity assumptions remain
necessary; selection into observed delivery records also limits interpretation.

```{r estimation-methods}
analyze_pkh <- function(outcome, published_estimate, published_se) {
  iv_formula <- as.formula(paste(outcome, "~ pkh_by_this_wave +", iv_covariate_rhs,
                                  "| L07 +", iv_covariate_rhs))
  fit_iv <- ivreg(iv_formula, data = dat)
  iv_estimate <- unname(coef(fit_iv)["pkh_by_this_wave"])
  iv_se <- sqrt(vcovCL(fit_iv, cluster = dat$kecamatan,
                       type = "HC1", cadjust = TRUE)["pkh_by_this_wave", "pkh_by_this_wave"])

  old_plan <- plan()
  on.exit(plan(old_plan), add = TRUE)
  if (settings$workers == 1L) plan(sequential) else plan(multisession, workers = settings$workers)
  set.seed(20261102)
  fit_ps <- prince_BART(
    as.formula(paste(outcome, "~", covariate_rhs, "| L07 | pkh_by_this_wave")),
    data = dat, uptake_type = "binary", n_chains = settings$n_chains,
    workers = settings$workers, n_warmup = settings$n_warmup,
    n_samples = settings$n_samples, n_trees = settings$n_trees, keep_trees = FALSE
  )
  plan(sequential)
  chains <- lapply(fit_ps$chains, function(chain) {
    pc <- 1 - chain$p_a - chain$p_n
    rowSums(pc * (chain$m_y1c - chain$m_y0c)) / rowSums(pc)
  })
  tau <- unlist(chains, use.names = FALSE)
  critical <- qnorm(c(0.025, 0.975))
  comparison <- tibble(
    Method = c("Published 2SLS", "Reconstructed 2SLS", "princeBART mixed complier effect"),
    Estimate_pp = 100 * c(published_estimate, iv_estimate, mean(tau)),
    Lower_pp = 100 * c(published_estimate + critical[1] * published_se,
                       iv_estimate + critical[1] * iv_se, quantile(tau, 0.025)),
    Upper_pp = 100 * c(published_estimate + critical[2] * published_se,
                       iv_estimate + critical[2] * iv_se, quantile(tau, 0.975)),
    Interval = c("95% CI (reconstructed)", "95% clustered CI", "95% CrI")
  )
  draws <- as_draws_array(array(unlist(chains),
    c(length(chains[[1]]), length(chains), 1),
    dimnames = list(NULL, NULL, "Complier effect")))
  segments <- segment_heterogeneity(
    fit_ps, rpart_control = rpart::rpart.control(cp = 0, maxdepth = 2),
    min_compliers_bucket = 50, ci_level = 0.95, plot = TRUE
  )
  list(comparison = comparison,
       diagnostics = summarise_draws(draws) |> select(variable, rhat, ess_bulk, ess_tail),
       effects = as_tibble(segments$effects) |>
         select(segment, mean, ci_lower, ci_upper, n, n_group),
       plot = segments$plot$effect)
}
```

# Objective 1: Skilled birth attendance

## 2SLS and princeBART comparison

```{r assisted-delivery}
assisted <- analyze_pkh("good_assisted_delivery", published_estimate = 0.233, published_se = 0.059)
assisted$comparison
assisted$diagnostics
```

## Effect heterogeneity

```{r assisted-heterogeneity}
assisted$effects
assisted$plot
```

# Objective 2: Delivery at a health facility

## 2SLS and princeBART comparison

```{r facility-delivery}
facility <- analyze_pkh("delivery_facility", published_estimate = 0.171, published_se = 0.066)
facility$comparison
facility$diagnostics
```

## Effect heterogeneity

```{r facility-heterogeneity}
facility$effects
facility$plot
```

Segment effects and their 95% credible intervals are probability differences.
These post hoc summaries describe the fitted effect curves; they do not confirm
subgroup differences or account for selection of the tree from the same data.
